title: UPSC CSE - Indian Economy - Budget Indirect Taxes GST
subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
What is/are the most likely advantages of implementing 'Goods and Services Tax (GST)'?
1. It will replace multiple taxes collected by multiple authorities and will thus create a single market in India.
2. It will drastically reduce the 'Current Account Deficit' of India and will enable it to increase its foreign exchange reserves.
3. It will enormously increase the growth and size of the economy of India and will enable it to overtake China in the near future.
questions.explain: GST has subsumed the majority of indirect taxes and now acts as a unified indirect tax with common tax rates across the country, allowing for seamless movement of goods and factors of production across states, effectively creating a single national market. GST is a domestic indirect tax and there is no such stated advantage that it drastically reduces the 'Current Account Deficit' or enables India to overtake China in the near future.

questions.q: The sales tax you pay while purchasing a toothpaste is:
options: tax imposed by the Central Government
tax imposed by the Central Government but collected by the State Government
tax imposed by the State Government but collected by Central Government
tax imposed and collected by State Government
questions.explain: Sales tax was an indirect tax imposed on the trade of goods and services. Sales tax was imposed and collected by the respective State Government. However, for interstate trade there used to be the Central Sales Tax, which was imposed by the Central Government. The Goods and Service Tax introduced on 1st July 2017 replaced the sales tax regime and has now created a common national market based on the principles of one nation one market.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of Value Added Tax?
options: It is a multi-point destination-based system of tax.
It is a tax levied on value addition at each stage of transaction in the production distribution chain.
It is a tax on the final consumption of goods or services and must ultimately be borne by the consumer.
It is basically a subject of the Central Government, and the State Governments are only a facilitator for its successful implementation.
questions.explain: Value Added Tax or VAT was an indirect tax levied on goods and services on each point of value addition in the production cycle. It is a multipoint destination-based system of tax, borne by the consumer on consuming final goods and services. VAT is entirely a subject of the State Government, not the Central Government. The VAT system is enforced by the State governments and the rates of taxation vary from state to state.
